standard.when: Only work that repeats what NexKit already does, in the same way: a change to docs, skills or tests only, or a fix inside one module that follows a pattern the module already has. It changes no decision of the engine, no prompt, no protocol schema, no config key or command, and nothing about tokens, secrets, markers, redaction or who may run a command. Anything else is hard.

hard.when: Everything that is not standard. That covers a change to the engine's states or decisions, the protocol's schemas, the GitHub host's calls of the engine, the import of NexKit 6's markers, prompts and their goldens, runtimes and pins, publishing, merging, retries and autopilot, and anything a mistake in which could let an agent write with a token, leak a secret, pass a marker that NexKit did not write, or start, repeat or merge work no rule allows. When unsure between standard and hard, choose hard.

checklist: The change keeps every rule of docs/writing-docs.md and leaves no doc statement false: read the page, its Decisions section and how the docs stay correct included, and check the diff, code included, against each of its rules
The change keeps docs/testing.md#rules-for-tests: read that section and check the tests and checks the change adds, changes or removes against each of its rules
The change keeps docs/security.md: read the page and check the diff against each of its rules, on untrusted input, agent output, markers, repository code, the Actions bot and secrets

The change keeps every Agreed decision in docs/decisions/ whose subject it touches, such as D10 (only the engine decides) and D13 (how the pipeline writes): read docs/decisions.md, open each such decision and check the diff against it
The change keeps docs/delivery.md#releases: a change other than a release sets no version and adds no CHANGELOG.md entry

checklist.text: The change adds no exception to a check and loosens none, as docs/testing.md#rules-for-tests states
